title: RAL Mirror Bug
description: Diagnose a register model whose mirror disagrees with the DUT, using only the log and the prediction checklist, and fix each testbench fault until the run is clean.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the first failure
steps.instructions: Run `testbench_buggy.sv` as it is. Find the first `[RegModel]` error and write down: which register and fields differ, what the DUT holds, what the model believed, and at what time. Then list every access in the test that changed that register, and say which component started each one (the register model or the firmware sequence). Decide which prediction set-up would have missed one of those accesses, find where the environment chooses its set-up, and fix it so that every transfer on the bus is predicted. Rerun and confirm that this error is gone.

steps.title: Step 2: Chase the next symptom
steps.instructions: Rerun after your first fix and read the new error, if there is one. Note which fields differ and by how much. Ask how many times the failing access must have been predicted to give that mirror, and list everything in the environment that can predict an access the register model starts. Fix the cause, not the symptom: do not change the field's policy or make it volatile. If your run is already clean of this kind of error, explain in one sentence why your step 1 fix also prevented it.

steps.title: Step 3: When the read was right but the mirror was not
steps.instructions: A remaining error appears right after a read whose value the test checked and accepted. Rerun with `+UVM_VERBOSITY=UVM_HIGH` and compare the predictor's `REG_PREDICT` line for that read with the value `read()` returned. Work out which component produced the value the predictor used, and fix that component. Rerun.

steps.title: Step 4: Prove it
steps.instructions: Run until the report summary shows `UVM_ERROR :    0` and `UVM_FATAL :    0` and the log ends with `[TEST] register checks complete`. For each fix, write one sentence naming the checklist question it answers. Then undo each fix on its own and confirm that its original symptom comes back, so you know every check can fail.
